title: Clopen inverse-image bijections detect homeomorphisms on spectral component spaces
statement: Let $T$ and $S$ be spectral topological spaces [def-weil-spectral-space], and let $f:T\to S$ be continuous. For a space $Z$, let $\operatorname{Clop}(Z)$ denote its subsets which are both open and closed, and let $\pi_0(Z)$ be the set of connected components (maximal connected subsets), with the quotient topology for the map $q_Z$ sending a point to its component. Suppose that inverse image $f^{-1}:\operatorname{Clop}(S)\to\operatorname{Clop}(T)$ is bijective. Then the map $\pi_0(f):\pi_0(T)\to\pi_0(S)$, sending the component of $t$ to the component of $f(t)$, is a homeomorphism. Its normalization is $\pi_0(f)q_T=q_Sf$. Empty spaces are allowed.

source.place: Agent consequence of Tag 0906 (lemma-spectral-pi0), Tag 005F (lemma-connected-component-intersection), and Tag 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering); the clopen-preimage criterion is not itself a quoted Stacks lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-component-quotient-clopen-naturality] to the given continuous map $f:T\to S$. With $P=\pi_0(T)$ and $Q=\pi_0(S)$ it supplies the continuous map $h:P\to Q$ sending the component of $t$ to that of $f(t)$, with $h q_T=q_S f$. Its natural clopen equivalence transfers the assumed bijectivity of $f^{-1}$ on clopens to bijectivity of $h^{-1}:\operatorname{Clop}(Q)\to\operatorname{Clop}(P)$.

source.place: Agent component-quotient functoriality and natural clopen descent, expanding the clopen-saturation passage in Tag 0900 (lemma-pi0-profinite), proof. This statement does not claim the profiniteness conclusion of that tag.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite] separately to the spectral spaces $T$ and $S$. It gives compactness, Hausdorffness and total disconnectedness of $P$ and $Q$, exactly the space hypotheses of the next step; it requires no spectral-map hypothesis on $f$.

Apply [lem-sfb-profinite-clopen-pullback-bijective-open] to $h$, with continuity and the clopen inverse-image bijection from step 1 and both profinite-space hypotheses from step 2. It gives that $h$ is bijective and open, including when a space is empty.

source.place: Agent separation and finite-subcover consequence of Tag 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering), using its pointwise clopen-basis consequence. This statement is not the finite-refinement assertion of the tag.

proof.text: The set-theoretic inverse $h^{-1}:Q\to P$ is continuous: for every open $O\subseteq P$, its inverse image under this inverse function is $h(O)$, open by step 3. Thus $h$ is a homeomorphism. Step 1 identifies this very map with $\pi_0(f)$ and retains the required normalization. No point was chosen from an empty space.

source.place: Agent assembly: open continuous bijections have continuous inverses, directly by the definition of continuity.

proof_origin.place: Assembly of natural clopen descent, Tag 0906 (lemma-spectral-pi0), and the clopen separation / finite-subcover argument based on Tag 08ZZ (lemma-profinite-refine-open-covering).
